- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–3% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; use 14-day EMA or 7-day rolling average to dampen volatility.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, model often misses the momentum; forecast should rise 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.3), model is prone to oscillation; use median of recent 5-day forecast instead of 30-day projection.
